first.rationale: Activation is down 6% QoQ, which is the most direct measurable decline among the three concurrent pressures. Memory_91 showed that in-product activation messaging improved week-one engagement and first meaningful action. This addresses the immediate activation drop without the revenue-quality risks of promotional_pricing (memory_73 showed retention harm) or the uncertain applicability of referral_incentives to new accounts. Onboarding simplification (memory_86, memory_31) is also relevant given the 4% completion decline, but activation messaging has more direct recent evidence and can be implemented faster. Enterprise_sales_assist targets a different segment (memory_44 applies to enterprise prospects specifically) and doesn't address the SMB activation decline. Verifying memory_86 and memory_91 will confirm the magnitude and durability of the earlier activation and onboarding effects before committing. A standard_experiment scale is appropriate: large enough to detect the 6% delta, small enough to preserve the option to pivot if early signals disappoint.

final.rationale: Archive verification confirms both memories. Memory_91 (in-product activation messaging) showed +6% activation and +1% retention with no downside. Memory_86 (shortened onboarding) showed +13% completion, -2.1 day time-to-value, and +3% retention. Activation is down 6% QoQ; this is the primary lever. While onboarding completion is also down 4%, the activation_messaging intervention has direct evidence of closing that exact gap and is faster to deploy. The verified +6% activation lift from memory_91 directly addresses the current 6% QoQ decline. Promotional_pricing carries documented retention risk (memory_73) and is strategically incompatible with sustainable revenue growth during competitive pressure. Referral_incentives work for established customers (memory_57) but lack evidence for new account acquisition at the necessary scale. A standard_experiment allows measurement against the 6% baseline decline while preserving ability to layer onboarding simplification later if needed. This decision maximizes sustainable qualified revenue by addressing activation decay with proven, low-risk intervention.
